This needs some testing. Does the persistent file still work after this change ?

yeah, I tested the changes by performing a Redfish PATCH. I confirmed the bmcweb_persistent_data.json was updated. After a systemctl restart bmcweb, the settings persisted, confirming that the static getPath() correctly identifies and loads the file using the new logic.

Please add to the commit msg 
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/9ad2c6f422bc0860314b853c287283dcbd29430d/docs/TESTING.md?plain=1#L1

https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/224f278c74a574962a74a7498a86989a360666ea/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L262
This is persistent data, you need to test some amount of rebooting and persistency.
Acknowledged

We typically avoid the ternary operator in bmcweb. I don't find this code easier to read or understand. 

Can you incorporate filesystem::path in with the ternary operator?
Yeah, I updated this patch without ternary operator
Acknowledged
The exiting code already caches the result in a static local variable, so I'm confused how this changed things.
yeah, here my aim only adding std::filesystem static variable already existing.
Of this patch, the only thing I think that's better is using std::filesystem::path rather than a string.  The rest seems like it's making the code more complex.
Why was this function renamed?
The rename is the consolidation of two functions (getStateFile and filename) into a single (getPath()). here both filename and state Dir we define and get
Acknowledged
Please don't create inline lambdas with no captures.  The previous code used a normal function and was easier to read.
Acknowledged. I have removed the inline lambda. The logic is now handled with a standard if check and a local static variable.
